citation: Cowles, Henry Chandler. The Physiographic Ecology of Chicago and Vicinity; A Study of the Origin, Development, and Classification of Plant Societies. Botanical Gazette 31 (1901): 73-108, 145-182.
author: Henry Chandler Cowles
locator: part 2, Botanical Gazette 31:145-182, the beach, dune and prairie societies
rights_note: Published 1901; JSTOR Early Journal Content, released for unrestricted use.
access_notes: Full text of part 2 retrieved and read on 2026-08-10: the middle beach carries 'a vegetation of xerophytic annuals, the most prominent of which is Cakile Americana'; Ammophila builds dunes 'extensive but low' through 'strong horizontal rhizome propagation'; Populus monilifera (P. deltoides) makes smaller but higher dunes and is frequent on the shifting sand; and on the lake plain 'Sedges encroach rapidly upon the bulrushes... and grasses in turn encroach upon the sedges, forming a prairie'.
note: Landform-by-landform plant societies for exactly this geography, written by the founder of the field. It is a 1901 observation, not an 1835 one, so it supports community composition by inference and never documents what stood on the site in the scene year.
